coverage_evidence.finding: the only behavioural guard for the near-discrete failure was withdrawn as non-scale-invariant, so the conditional normality assumption is unguarded in the low-support regime

withdrawn_guard.behavioural_effect_now: none. The count is computed for reporting and no branch reads it: it does not affect support, the critical value, the bounds or the outcome. A behavioural scale-invariance test enforces this.
withdrawn_guard.how_it_is_handled_instead: a data-independent design-state precondition. While interval_criterion_registration.registered is false, --run refuses BEFORE any analysis, so the suspension cannot be triggered by, or confused with, a statistic computed from the data.
replacement_requirements: scale invariant across components spanning many orders of magnitude
independently justified, not selected by testing candidates against job 62960056
pre-registered in this spec and hash-bound before any confirmatory run
accompanied by a measured coverage study under the same four error laws
withdrawn_guard.what_is_now_unguarded: under a near-discrete error law the Bonferroni component's coverage was measured at 0.0283. No replacement guard exists, so this is an open limitation of the interval construction.
withdrawn_guard.what_it_was: a supported component whose absolute replicate standard deviation fell below 0.05 of the column median standard deviation blocked the comparison
withdrawn_guard.why_withdrawn: it is not scale invariant. The production observable is four wavelengths by thirty radial bins and spans 7.5 to 10.0 decades within a single column, so the outer bins have a genuinely tiny absolute spread because their signal is tiny, and the rule read that as a collapsed sample. In job 62960056 it fired on 26 to 29 components per column, every one below 1e-4 of the column maximum and none above 1e-2, and it blocked all five columns.

current_formulation.coverage_assumption: per-component approximate normality of the replicate values
current_formulation.coverage_method: larger of a Bonferroni-corrected t at alpha/(2m) on n-1 degrees of freedom and a centered sign-flip studentized-max quantile
current_formulation.statistic: max over retained components j of ( |mean_r (e3-e2)_rj| + c(n,k) se_j ) / max(|mean e2_j|, |mean e3_j|)
current_formulation.why_not_registered: the route relies on an unguarded approximate-normality assumption in the measured low-support regime and all five historical columns remain unresolved under that assumption

decision.future_reopening_condition: an independently justified error model or exact low-count construction, a predeclared support contract propagated through downstream Fisher analyses, and a newly frozen validation design
decision.reason: the route relies on an unguarded approximate-normality assumption exactly where nominal support is sparse, is not compatible with the literal full observable without a consequential support change, and all five historical columns remain unresolved even under that assumption

support.note: this is the support the formal run actually used. Any calculation that retains a literal 120 for every column, mus_slope included, is a SEPARATE post-hoc diagnostic and is not the support of the formal run.
support.rule: a component is excluded only when BOTH the reference and the quantity being checked are at or below 1e-12 of the largest magnitude across components

low_support_audit.interpretation: nominal support remains sparse in the outer bins even after pooling the six historical replicates; this is a support diagnostic, not a proof of any derivative error law
